newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to launch Nasdaq-like bolsa for smaller cos.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to launch Nasdaq-like bolsa for smaller cos.

text.p: Brazilian stock exchanges joined forces to launch a Nasdaq-like bourse for emerging companies in the first half of October, an official for Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange (BVRJ) said.

The new bolsa, called SOMA, is aimed at encouraging small and medium-sized companies to launch initial public offerings and organizing Brazil's over-the-counter market, said the BVRJ official who asked not to be named.
Companies with annual gross revenues of up to 100 million reais will qualify to be traded on the bourse, he said.
Currently, there are 800 public companies, of which 550 are listed, totalling 1,300 preferred and common stocks traded on the stock exchanges.
"Approximately 250 companies may be traded on the Nasdaq-like bourse," he added.

SOMA was founded by the BVRJ and other bourses across the country, except Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa), the National Development Bank (BNDES), National Association of Investment Banks (Anbid), Association of Brokerage Houses (Adeval), Brazilian Association of Public Companies (Abrasca) and the National Association of Market Makers.
The Rio bourse will provide operational infrastructure, while the CLC clearing house will provide custody and settlement services, the official said.
